result:
I’ll trace scorer reconstruction and guardrail loading, add the server-side protections, and run focused tests. I’m using the repository’s Python style skill for the code and test changes.
Scorer reconstruction is centralized, so the refusal can be enforced there. I’ll preserve custom scorers as metadata in the server and use an in-process executor flag, rather than an environment variable, to allow reconstruction in job workers.
The working tree already has staged regression tests for this change. I’ll preserve them and implement the behavior they cover. They also identify a scheduler case: disabled custom scorers must be skipped so they don’t prevent built-in scorers from being scheduled.
The core protections are implemented. The new reconstruction tests passed in the first run, but unrelated trace tests failed because their fixtures returned no trace. I’ve narrowed the next run to scorer reconstruction, scheduling, server startup, and guardrails, including workspace-enabled storage tests.
The focused guardrail run now passes its test cases, including nested custom scorers, workspace-aware creation, and HTTP 500 responses for existing unsafe guardrails. Other loading errors still get logged and skipped. I also added checks for metadata preservation and source that would execute while rebuilding a function.

The test summary hook hits a sandbox permission error when inspecting child processes; that is separate from the test results.
Implemented inert custom-scorer loading in the server, with reconstruction and execution blocked. Job executors and clients retain execution support, and server startup clears inherited executor permission.

Custom guardrails—including ensembles—are rejected. Existing unsafe guardrails now produce HTTP 500 errors naming the guardrail; unrelated loading failures remain logged and skipped.

Added regression coverage. Focused runs passed 127 and 14 test cases, though the summary hook hit a sandbox permission error. Broader runs also encountered unrelated trace-fixture failures. No dependencies installed or full suite run.
